text: The clinic is located in Soi Ladprao 101 (you can also access it via Soi Pho Kaew on Nawamin Road), right in front of Wat Bueng Thonglang Secondary School, easily visible. Parking can be a bit difficult though. A colleague recommended it, saying the service was excellent, so I decided to try it. I've been an orthodontic patient here for 3.5 years now. I'd give it 10 out of 10 stars, and I'd even give it 11! I was impressed from the very first visit, especially during the oral preparation. Initially, I was prepared for significant pain due to my childhood experiences, but meeting the dentist here completely changed my perspective. I realized oral health is a personal and important matter that everyone should prioritize and shouldn't neglect. I've overcome my fear of dentists. The dentists here are experienced, gentle, and fully equipped. They provide clear explanations and answer questions accurately, predicting future progress with noticeable monthly updates. The assistants are friendly and welcoming, and the fees are reasonable – excellent value for money. The atmosphere before, during, and after treatments is consistently high. If you live nearby or are looking for a good dental clinic, I highly recommend this one. You won't be disappointed.

text:
Added on 8/14/2024
I'd like to respond to the clinic's clarification. **Since there's no space to write a reply, I'll provide more clarification in my original review instead.
**Thank you to the clinic for your concern and for clarifying the facts. I also thank the clinic's owner for taking care of me. However, I won't be going back for treatment because:
1. I had the tooth extracted at another clinic and, while waiting for the wound to heal, I'll have to get a denture.
2. I'd like to clarify that it's indeed the same tooth I had filled that day, but the filling didn't reach the cavity. I asked the doctor who extracted the tooth. The doctor didn't mention the previous clinic, probably out of medical ethics. However, I was curious, so I asked the doctor if this was the tooth I just had filled. The doctor said yes, but the filling didn't reach the cavity, which is why I felt pain when eating. (This is my personal opinion, based on my experience with the extracted tooth, as someone with no knowledge of fillings. I feel like the previous doctor probably filled the top, not the inside, in the gap between the tooth I mentioned. The cavity wasn't small. The unfilled cavity was very visible if you really look closely, as I mentioned.) That day, I probably saw the hole in the crevice between my teeth.)
**I'd like to thank the clinic again for taking the time to write this review. Thank you so much.

I usually get my teeth done here. I'm covered by the Social Security Fund, and the service is generally good. Sometimes, sometimes, sometimes not. I'll switch to another clinic every year, but this year, I got my teeth filled here. I paid for it myself, not covered by the Social Security Fund. *Not* impressed at all. I felt really bad this time. I had a filling on my back molar with a hole on the side, and food kept getting stuck. I had to floss to get it out, but there were no other symptoms. There was no pain, no sensitivity, and I could eat and chew normally. However, I was afraid that leaving it too long would cause problems later on, so I made an appointment with the staff to get the filling. I told the doctor and the staff about the problem and the filling. The doctor filled my tooth. After the filling, I felt sensitive, which wasn't normal. The doctor was a bit moody while doing it, yelling at the assistants, and he used a stern voice. In the end, I paid 1,000 baht for the filling. When I got home, my tooth was sensitive more often, and even more so. I thought it was normal, a symptom after the filling. After a month, it still hadn't gone away, so I went back to the same doctor. After some examination, the assistant found a sensitive spot in my tooth. The doctor couldn't find it. As soon as he found it, the doctor politely said that he hadn't done it on this tooth. I told him that I would only do this one that day. The doctor said he hadn't done it, so there must be another tooth that was more sensitive, so he hadn't done it on this one. The doctor emphasized several times that he hadn't done it. He asked me if I wanted to fill the sensitive tooth and there would be a fee. I told him no, but I wouldn't do it yet. When I got home, I opened my mouth to see which tooth I had filled that day. The white-cream filling material was stuck to the sensitive tooth, but the doctor said he hadn't done it. To be honest, if a doctor is going to fill a tooth that a patient doesn't want to do, shouldn't they have to talk to the patient and explain it first? Or if the doctor really has a problem with the filling, just admit it and fix it for the patient and that's it. Doctors are people, and mistakes are inevitable. But this time, the doctor insisted that he hadn't done it. Oh, and the day I went back to see the same doctor, I had to pay 50 baht for sterilization. The pain came back even worse than before. From just a little pain, it started to throbbing. I don't know if it was from the equipment the doctor used to test the sensitivity or what the cause was, but this time, life was harder than before. It was difficult to eat anything. My teeth were sensitive. But I'm just an ordinary patient. I don't think I have anything to fight or complain to the doctor about. The only thing you can do is consult with someone else to fix it. Consider it a bad omen.
